as_told.title: Bondi's question on positivity conditions at Chapel Hill

plain: At a 1957 physics conference in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, the meeting Jesse Michels credits with founding the study of quantum gravity, an Austrian mathematician named Hermann Bondi gave a talk on negative mass in general relativity: matter with a minus sign that would push against gravity rather than fall with it. Michels says he got this from the mathematician Eric Weinstein, who frames Bondi's point as a question about whether mass must always be positive, and Michels says he has the conference report, The Role of Gravitation in Physics, which has a chapter on the talk. He raises it as a hint that serious physicists looked at antigravity long ago.
